facts.text: Concrete earned its name when two neighboring cement towns merged in 1909, choosing the industry’s moniker to honor the Washington Portland Cement Company.
The Henry Thompson Bridge, finished 1916‑18, crosses the Skagit River and commemorates a settler killed by a logging train.
Every May, Concrete hosts the Mountain Film Festival, a three‑day celebration of mountain life and outdoor recreation.
Concrete’s Historic Preservation and Landmarks Commission meets monthly on the fourth Wednesday at 6 p.m. in Town Hall.
Concrete sits in the North Cascades, just southeast of Mount Baker and almost directly south of Mount Shuksan.
The town is restoring the historic Superior Building, a landmark that once housed the Washington Portland Cement Company’s factory.
